close_reason: Rewrote the README example to be a complete fn main() with explicit return type and ? operator inside the function body. Copy-paste now compiles standalone. Removed the cryptic '# Ok::<(), serde_json::Error>(())' rustdoc-hidden-line that doesn't render in plain markdown README.
description:
crate-jmap-jscalendar-types/README.md lines 51-61 show:

```rust
use jmap_jscalendar_types::RecurrenceRule;
use serde_json::json;

let rule: RecurrenceRule = serde_json::from_value(json!({...}))?;
# Ok::<(), serde_json::Error>(())
```

The '# Ok::<()>' line is a rustdoc-hidden marker that is meaningful inside //! doc-comments processed by cargo doc, but not in a standalone README.md. README.md is rendered by crates.io and GitHub, where:

- the '#' line is shown verbatim (looks like a comment)
- the surrounding 'let rule = ...?' is not inside a fn, so a reader who copies it into 'fn main() { ... }' gets 'error[E0277]: the ? operator can only be used in a function that returns Result' because main returns ().

Comparable precedent: JMAP-6xs8.1 (README.md JmapRequest example fails to compile outside crate) was filed P0 for the foundation crate jmap-types because the README is a primary consumer touch point. Lower priority here because (a) this crate's docs are not embedded via #[doc = include_str!("README.md")] (verified — lib.rs has no include_str), (b) the snippet is illustrative not a quick-start.

Two options:

(a) Wrap the snippet in 'fn main() -> Result<(), serde_json::Error> { ... ; Ok(()) }' so a verbatim copy compiles. Drop the rustdoc hidden line.

(b) Mark the block as 'ignore' (```rust,ignore) so readers know not to expect it to compile standalone, and drop the rustdoc hidden line.

Recommendation: (a) — the snippet is short, the wrap is one extra line, and it gives the reader a runnable example.
title: README.md example snippet uses ? operator outside fn — copy-paste yields E0277
